questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Slow the engine and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Why should you use both brakes every time you slow down or stop?

options.text: Using only one brake will wear them unevenly.
It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
You cannot slow down a motorcycle without using both brakes.
The brakes only work when both are applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops builds a habit of always using both. This habit is critical in emergencies when you need both brakes to stop safely.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
Passing should be done on the shoulder, not the main road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are harder to see than cars because they are smaller. Drivers may not notice you or may not see you if you are in their blind spot.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees the driver will yield to you.
It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
It means the driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means another driver will properly yield to you. They may not yield even if they look at you.

questions.question: Which of these is not a good way to increase visibility?

options.text: Use your headlight at all times

questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light correctly. Waving is not an effective way to increase visibility.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, even if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Focus only on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers may look directly at you and still not see you. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: When choosing clothes for riding, which is not a good choice?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles

questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not provide proper protection.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should not:
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently if needed. Do not brake quickly.

questions.question: Which of these provides the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time. Apply them firmly. Do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake of the tire that is flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat (if you are sure which one it is).

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?

options.text: From a library book about motorcycles.

questions.explanation: The owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. Read the manual before you ride your motorcycle for the first time.

questions.question: To avoid serious injury, you should wear protective gear. Which item is NOT necessary?
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of sturdy material, high and sturdy boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding because it will likely stop on its own.
Close the throttle to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, lean forward and down with your weight, and pull off the road as soon as possible. Once off the road, find and fix the cause of the wobble.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, where should you place it?

options.text: Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Place loads low on your motorcycle. Placing them high, such as on a sissy bar, raises the center of gravity and makes the motorcycle harder to balance. Spread the load evenly on both sides to avoid pulling the bike to one side.

questions.question: What might happen if you ride in cold weather for a long time? Which is NOT a risk?
questions.explanation: Long rides in cold weather can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, how should they pass?

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.

questions.explanation: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. One rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: How often should you check your motorcycle mirrors?

options.text: More often than you look ahead

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see what is behind you and to be aware of possible hazards.

questions.question: What should a good face shield NOT be?

options.text: Allow clear views to both sides.

questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, resist penetration, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, and permit air to pass through. A face shield should NOT be airtight because trapped air causes fogging and makes it hard to see.
